messages:
alex: heads-up — console alert for Dedicated us-east-1 GPU pool: p99 latency for text-gen spiked from 120ms -> 780ms over last 10m. seeing packet-loss on east-west between nodes. https://console.redwood/alerts/INC-8421 :signal_strength:
infra-bot: alert INC-8421 created by latency-slo-checker (p99 > 500ms on route /v1/generate)
sri: can you dump `tc` on one of the affected hosts? suspect host shaping/QoS
alex: grabbing one now, pasted below:
```
$ sudo tc qdisc show dev eth0
qdisc fq_codel 8022: root refcnt 2 limit 10240 target 20ms interval 100ms
qdisc ingress ffff: dev eth0 parent ffff:fff1
```
$ sudo tc -s qdisc show dev eth0
qdisc fq_codel 8022: root refcnt 2 limit 10240 target 20ms interval 100ms
 Sent 123456789 bytes  packets 987654
 backlog 0b requeues 0
  drops 312 packets  errors 0
```
alex: iperf between two nodes shows ~0.6% packet loss, high retransmits.
marco: that's a lot of drops for inner-cluster RPCs. Why is fq_codel on the host with such a tight target? our default bake shouldn't put shaping on worker NICs.
sri: checking AMI provisioner scripts — there's a recent change in provisioner v2.3.4 that adds `tc qdisc add dev eth0 root fq_codel limit 10240 target 20ms` to limit bursting during noisy tenants. looks like it rolled out to Dedicated images last night.
alex: reproducing quick mitigation: `sudo tc qdisc del dev eth0 root` on one host — p99 for that host's instances dropped back to ~140ms within 30s. confirming across 3 nodes. :white_check_mark:
ops-oncall: good quick fix. we should rollback the AMI change and do a controlled rollout. Also need postmortem for SLO hit window.
marco: agreed. short-term: 1) remove qdisc on all active nodes in pool (or restart network service), 2) roll AMI back, 3) add gating test to bake that runs intra-cluster iperf + tc mismatch check.
sri: proposal for long-term: replace blanket fq_codel with cake + per-tenant rate-limit where we actually shape egress to external networks, not east-west internal fabric. fq_codel on worker NICs causes kernel-level drops that our RPC transport interprets as server-side stalls.
alex: adding commands we used:
```
# show
sudo tc -s qdisc show dev eth0
# remove
sudo tc qdisc del dev eth0 root
# re-add safe mode (if needed)
sudo tc qdisc add dev eth0 root cake bandwidth 0pps
```
sri: also caught that target was set to 20ms (higher than default 5ms) — with our tiny RPCs that increases queueing and drop-priority for bursts. fq_codel drops can be observed as retransmits in application logs. add a tracer to inference runtime to correlate `tcp_retransmits` with token P99.
ops-oncall: created ticket INFRA-1092 to roll back provisioner change and deploy a bake-test. assigning to @marco and @sri.
marco: I'll push a hotfix to the provisioner to remove the tc line and add a test in bake: verify no non-empty root qdisc on worker NICs and run a 60s iperf UDP test expecting <0.1% loss.
alex: we should also add a node-exporter gauge exposing `host_qdisc_mode{dev="eth0"}` and an alert when it != "none" on Dedicated pools. that would've caught the rollout mismatch earlier.
sri: +1. also add an alert for `node_tcp_retransmits_total` spike correlated with inference SLO violations.
ops-oncall: doing immediate remediation now (del on all nodes in pool). ETA 12m. will update ticket INFRA-1092 with timeline and postmortem owner.
alex: after removing qdisc on remaining nodes p99 recovered cluster-wide to ~130-160ms. closing the alert in console.
marco: follow-ups: PR to provisioner to remove shaping (will include cake option for edge gateways), bake test PR, monitoring PR for exporter + rules.
sri: note for docs: calling out pitfalls of host-level shaping with RDMA or kernel-bypass transports — masquerading as packet loss but actually induced by codel. add to runbook.
alex: thanks team — saved SLO. filing short incident note in #incidents. :thumbsup:
